title: The representer theorem: a minimal seed
scope: Minimal authoring example centered on the representer theorem of proof.md, with the training-span definition and projection lemma as selected prerequisites. The assumptions named in the synopses remain in the source at this seed stage. The captured export overview.json adds those assumptions and the kernel-ridge corollary to complete the example's selected argument.

statement.text: Under Assumption 1, $S=\operatorname{span}\{k_{x_1},\ldots,k_{x_n}\}\subseteq\mathcal H$ is the span of the kernel sections at the training inputs, a finite-dimensional hence closed subspace; $P_S$ is the orthogonal projection onto $S$.

Under Assumption 1 and Definition 2, every $f\in\mathcal H$ decomposes uniquely as $f=s+h$ with $s=P_Sf\in S$ and $h\in S^\perp$; moreover $f(x_i)=s(x_i)$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$ and $\|f\|_{\mathcal H}^2=\|s\|_{\mathcal H}^2+\|h\|_{\mathcal H}^2$.

Under Assumptions 1 and 3, if $J$ attains a finite minimum on $\mathcal H$, every minimizer $f_*$ belongs to the training span $S$: there are coefficients $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\in\mathbb R$ with $f_*(\cdot)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i k(\cdot,x_i)$.

uses.reason: The lemma's decomposition and projection $P_S$ are defined relative to the training span $S$.
The proof applies Lemma 4 to a minimizer $f_*=s+h$: equal training evaluations make the loss terms equal, and the norm identity with strict increase of $\Omega$ contradicts minimality unless $h=0$.
